evals.name: offline-channel-transfer
evals.prompt: write up a guide for getting kolibri channels onto the desktop when it has no internet - i'd download on my laptop and move them over by usb
evals.expected_output: A markdown doc in house style: numbered ## sections from 0, --- separators, per-step verification, troubleshooting table, and a dated verification status table marking unverified claims.
assertions: Every documented route has a check — including the alternative or fallback routes the document itself introduces. Offering the reader a route and no way to confirm it worked is a fail.
Each check names an observable signal the reader can actually see: a specific message, file, count or screen. 'It should now appear' without saying where to look is a fail.
Every exact flag, path, filename, port or menu label is either backed by a Verified row naming its source, or marked Unverified. Confidently-stated unsourced specifics are a fail.
The verification status table covers the specifics the procedure actually depends on. A table full of easy rows while the load-bearing detail goes unlisted is a fail.

scoring.note: Pass rate is computed over `assertions` only. `guards` are cheap script checks that catch regressions but passed in every run of iteration 1, so counting them diluted the delta from +0.67 to +0.17.
guards: A verification status table is present and dated
Top-level sections are numbered from 0 with --- separators
Prose is hard-wrapped at 80 columns (tables, code fences, headings, bare URLs exempt)
